jun: FYI I just finished a quick bring-up run for nebula-v2 (int8 quant) on the subtitle mixed-orientation testset and hit a weird bracket mirroring / ordering issue when Arabic spans are embedded inside CJK lines. Repro snippet below :eyes:

jun: example input (SRT line):

```
00:00:12,000 --> 00:00:15,000
東京の会議で彼はこう言った: (مرحبا) 『よろしくお願いします』
```

jun: Expected detok (baseline fp16/int8 shadow): Tokyo sentence with Arabic in parentheses, then Japanese corner quotes 「よろしくお願いします」. Observed (nebula-v2 int8): the parentheses around Arabic are mirrored and the CJK corner quotes get swapped order. Output: 

```
東京の会議で彼はこう言った: )مرحبا( 『お願いします よろしく』
```

mari: whoa. That's not just formatting — it changes token boundaries and BLEU. What are the numbers? :bug:

jun: quick eval numbers (mixed en/zh/ja + ar subs):
- baseline fp16: BLEU 28.5
- nebula-v2 int8 (current): BLEU 24.1
- nebula-v2 int4 (experimental): BLEU 28.3 (close to baseline)

jun: suggests the regression correlates with int8 quant path + detok routine that runs post-inference. Looks like directional mark / bracket class mapping gets flipped when we reassemble tokens.

akshay: can you paste tokenizer outputs for that input across the three builds? also include unicode codepoints for the quotes/parens.

jun: tokenizer dump (showing tokens + codepoints):

- Input tokens (baseline fp16): ["東京","の","会議","で","彼","は","こう","言った",":"," ","(","مرحبا",")"," ","『","よろしく","お願いします","』"]
- Codepoints: '(', U+0028; ')', U+0029; '『' U+300C; '』' U+300D; Arabic letters in U+0600..

- nebula-v2 int8 tokenizer (raw ids): [..] (same tokenization) — so tokenization not diverging.

jun: detok step (post-join) seems to reorder. I instrumented the detok function and saw it apply an RTL reflow pass that assumes parentheses are neutral and will mirror based on paragraph embedding. On int8 path the reflow pass ran after some byte-level rewrite (quantized kernel output) and appears to have lost explicit directionality markers (LRM/RLM) that baseline preserves.

mari: int4 passes — suggests the quant kernel differences cause elision of U+200F/U+200E markers or they get stripped by a C postprocessing step. akshay can you run the kernel with byte-trace?

akshay: will run. pinging @deploy-bot to spin a debug job on dedede (staging) with kernel trace and the failing SRT sample.

deploy-bot: job created: run-6851234567-debug-kern. logs will be in /runs/run-6851234567-debug-kern (link: https://staging.rw/run-6851234567-debug-kern)

qa-bot: quick smoke on staging run (partial): reproduced bracket mirror on int8 model but not on fp16 or int4. Attached minimal failing line and diff.

jun: minimal failing line to test locally: "東京: (שלום) 「ありがとう」"

mari: next steps proposed:
1) akshay — gather kernel trace and confirm if U+200E/U+200F or bidi class bytes are zeroed after quant kernels.
2) eng-runtime — gate the detok reflow to skip mirroring for mixed-orientation subtitle routes until we have a fix.
3) ml — run bisect between our int8 quantization passes (qconfig v1 -> v3) to find offending transform.
4) QA — expand smoke set to 200 SRT lines with mixed RTL/CJK spans.

akshay: ack, will post traces and a short perl/python snippet to check for removed directional markers.

jun: I also noticed the detok code has a special-case that tries to be clever with bracket pairs: it checks Unicode Bidi_Class on the first codepoint of the span and then may reverse pairs if bidi is RTL. That heuristic is fragile when a neutral punctuation sits between directional runs. Seems the quant kernel emits a slightly different byte sequence for neutral tokens which trips the heuristic.

mari: thanks. assigning follow-ups in the bug tracker and will open a short postmortem if this touches canary. For immediate mitigation I'll flip the route to use fp16 in dedicated for captioning customers.

jun: adding sample SRT bundle link: https://internal.rw/samples/mixed-orient-subtitles.zip

akshay: started traces, will report back ~2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mari: thx everyone. If anyone sees quick wins (detok guardrails) PRs welcome — tag me. :thumbsup:
